rows.question: When does my maternity leave start if my due date is 15 November 2026?
rows.reply:
Your Mutterschutz (statutory maternity protection period) before the birth covers the last six weeks before the expected delivery date. The law says the employer may not employ a pregnant woman "in den letzten sechs Wochen vor der Entbindung" (in the last six weeks before the birth), unless she expressly declares she is willing to work. She can withdraw that declaration at any time for the future.

The period is counted from the expected delivery date shown on the certificate from a doctor or midwife ("der voraussichtliche Tag der Entbindung ... wie er sich aus dem ärztlichen Zeugnis oder dem Zeugnis einer Hebamme ... ergibt"). Counting six weeks back from 15 November 2026 gives 4 October 2026. The excerpts do not set out the exact day-counting rule, so check the confirmed start date with your employer.

If the baby is not born on the expected date, the period before the birth becomes shorter or longer to match. After the birth, the protection period runs for eight weeks. It runs for twelve weeks after a premature birth or a multiple birth. If the baby comes early, the time lost before the birth is added to the period after it.

Self-employed women are not covered by the Mutterschutzgesetz.

rows.question: How long after birth can we apply for Elterngeld without losing money?
rows.reply:
The law does not set an application deadline. What it limits is back payment. Elterngeld (parental allowance) must be applied for in writing, and it is paid retroactively only for the last three months of the child's life before the start of the month of life in which the application is received. The German wording is: "Es wird rückwirkend nur für die letzten drei Lebensmonate vor Beginn des Lebensmonats geleistet, in dem der Antrag auf Elterngeld eingegangen ist." Months of life further back than those three are not paid.

This matters because Elterngeld can be drawn from the day of birth ("Es kann ab dem Tag der Geburt bezogen werden"). Elterngeld is paid in monthly amounts for the child's months of life. An application received after the first months of the child's life therefore loses whole months of payment.

The same three-month limit applies if you later change the months you chose in the application.

Which months are paid in your case is decided by your Elterngeldstelle, the office that handles Elterngeld applications.

rows.question: How much notice do I have to give my employer for Elternzeit?
rows.reply:
Elternzeit (parental leave (unpaid job-protected leave)) is requested from your employer in text form. The notice period depends on when the leave falls.

- Leave before the child's third birthday: at the latest seven weeks before the leave starts ("spätestens sieben Wochen").
- Leave between the third birthday and the end of the child's eighth year: at the latest 13 weeks before the leave starts ("spätestens 13 Wochen").

When you request leave for the period before the third birthday, you must also state at the same time which periods within two years you will take as Elternzeit.

In urgent cases, a reasonable shorter period is possible as an exception ("Bei dringenden Gründen ist ausnahmsweise eine angemessene kürzere Frist möglich"). The Familienportal gives premature births as one example and says the period that applies then depends on the individual case.

If a mother cannot request Elternzeit in time, for a reason she is not responsible for, for leave directly after the maternity protection period, she can make up the request within one week after that reason ends.

"Text form" means a signature is not needed. The Familienportal says a letter without a signature or an email is enough. Your employer must confirm your Elternzeit to you in writing ("Der Arbeitgeber hat ... die Elternzeit zu bescheinigen").

The Familienportal page also says that for children born before 1 July 2015, the notice period is seven weeks for all Elternzeit. The statutory transitional rule for those births is not in the excerpts I have, so I cannot confirm where its boundary lies. If this applies to you, check it with your employer or a labour law adviser.

rows.question: How long is maternity protection after the birth if the baby comes early?
rows.reply:
Mutterschutz (statutory maternity protection period) after the birth normally lasts eight weeks. During this time your employer may not employ you (MuSchG §3(2)).

If the baby comes early, two separate rules can apply.

1. Birth before the expected date. The period before the birth is cut short, because it is counted from the expected date of delivery. The law then adds the days that were lost to the period after the birth: "Bei vorzeitiger Entbindung verlängert sich die Schutzfrist nach der Entbindung … um den Zeitraum der Verkürzung der Schutzfrist vor der Entbindung" (MuSchG §3(1) and §3(2)). Familienportal explains that the total stays at 14 weeks. The period ends as many days after the eight weeks as the baby arrived before the expected date.

2. Premature birth in the medical sense. The period after the birth is extended to twelve weeks "bei Frühgeburten" (MuSchG §3(2)). The days lost before the birth are added on top of these twelve weeks, under the same rule as above. Familienportal describes a premature birth as one that counts as premature medically, for example a birth weight under 2,500 grams. It says this raises the total period from 14 to 18 weeks.

The same twelve-week extension also applies to multiple births. It also applies where a disability in the child is medically established within the first eight weeks, but only if you apply for it (MuSchG §3(2)).

These excerpts do not say who decides whether a birth counts as premature. Your health insurance fund (Krankenkasse) or your employer can confirm how the period is applied in your case.

rows.question: Can my employer dismiss me while I am pregnant?
rows.reply:
In general, no. The law says dismissal of a woman by her employer is not permitted ("Die Kündigung gegenüber einer Frau ist unzulässig"):

- during her pregnancy;
- until the end of her protection period after the birth, and at least until four months after the birth;
- until four months after a miscarriage after the twelfth week of pregnancy.

This Kündigungsschutz (protection against dismissal) applies if the employer knows about the pregnancy when giving notice, or is told within two weeks of receiving the notice. Missing those two weeks does no harm if it was not your fault and you inform the employer without delay ("unverzüglich"). According to the official family portal, the protection also applies if you did not yet know you were pregnant, but you must already have been pregnant when you received the notice.

There is one exception. In special cases that are not connected with the pregnancy, a miscarriage or the birth, the state's highest authority responsible for occupational safety, or a body it designates, can exceptionally declare a dismissal permissible. Such a dismissal must be in writing and must state the reason. The family portal gives examples such as insolvency, partial closure of the business, or a particularly serious breach of duty. Without the authority's approval, the dismissal is invalid.

If you are dismissed without that approval, the family portal says you must bring a claim before the competent labour court, "normalerweise innerhalb von 3 Wochen" (normally within 3 weeks) from receiving the written notice. If you do not bring a claim, the employer's dismissal is treated as valid. The portal also says you should involve the responsible supervisory authority.

If you later take parental leave, a separate protection against dismissal applies from the time the leave is requested and during the leave.

Whether a particular dismissal is permissible is decided by the state authority responsible for occupational safety, and whether a dismissal is valid is decided by the labour court.

rows.question: Is there an income limit above which we get no Elterngeld?
rows.reply:
Yes. Under the statute, there is no entitlement to Elterngeld (parental allowance) above a certain level of zu versteuerndes Einkommen (taxable income).

BEEG §1(8) says the entitlement lapses ("Ein Anspruch entfällt") if the entitled person had taxable income of more than 175,000 euros ("mehr als 175 000 Euro") in the last completed tax assessment period before the child's birth. If another person also meets the conditions, the entitlement lapses when both persons' taxable income together is more than 175,000 euros ("die Summe des zu versteuernden Einkommens beider Personen mehr als 175 000 Euro").

The limit is based on zu versteuerndes Einkommen, not gross income. The official Familienportal explains that gross income is usually considerably higher than taxable income. The Finanzamt determines your taxable income, and it appears in your Steuerbescheid (tax assessment notice).

If the tax assessment for the last completed period before the birth is not yet available, BEEG §8 still lets you apply. If the application indicates the limit will probably not be exceeded, Elterngeld is paid subject to revocation if the limit turns out to be exceeded. If it cannot yet be stated whether the limit is exceeded, the decision is provisional until the required information is provided.

The Familienportal also says that different limits applied to earlier births. The excerpts do not include the statutory transitional provision for those births, so I cannot say where its boundaries lie. Which limit applies to a particular birth, and whether a particular family is above or below it, is decided only by the responsible Elterngeldstelle.

rows.question: How many months of Elterngeld can we get in total?
rows.reply:
The law sets the total in months of Elterngeld (parental allowance), counted by the child's months of life. Which months your family actually receives is decided by your Elterngeldstelle, not by this explanation.

The basic rule:
- Parents together are entitled to 12 monthly payments of basic Elterngeld.
- They get 2 more months (partner months) if one parent's earned income is reduced in two months of the child's life. That makes 14 months to share.
- One parent can receive at most 12 months of basic Elterngeld, plus up to 4 partnership bonus months.
- A parent only has a claim if they receive Elterngeld for at least two months.

Swapping for the Plus variant: instead of one month of basic Elterngeld, a parent can take two months of Elterngeld Plus. This stretches the same entitlement over a longer period.

Partnership bonus: the official family portal explains that each parent can get up to 4 extra months of Elterngeld Plus if both work part-time at the same time.

Time limits on when months can be taken:
- Basic Elterngeld can only be received until the child completes the 14th month of life.
- Elterngeld Plus can be received until the child completes the 32nd month of life, as long as from the 15th month at least one parent takes it in consecutive months. The family portal says that if there is a month after the 14th in which neither parent receives it, no more can be received afterwards, even with months left over.

Months that count as used: for the mother, months in which she receives maternity benefits count as months of basic Elterngeld, whether or not she applies for them.

Premature births: if the child was born at least 6, 8, 12 or 16 weeks before the expected delivery date, the joint entitlement rises to 13, 14, 15 or 16 monthly payments of basic Elterngeld respectively. The expected date on the doctor's or midwife's certificate is what counts.

When you apply, the application must state for which months of life you claim basic Elterngeld, Elterngeld Plus or partnership bonus.

How these rules apply to your family is decided by your Elterngeldstelle.

rows.question: What is the Partnerschaftsbonus and who qualifies?
rows.reply:
The Partnerschaftsbonus (partnership bonus months) is an extra payment of parental allowance in its 'Plus' form, for parents who both work part-time at the same time.

What the law says (BEEG §4b):
- If both parents work, on average over the child's month of life, no less than 24 and no more than 32 hours a week ("nicht weniger als 24 und nicht mehr als 32 Wochenstunden im Durchschnitt des Lebensmonats"), and both meet the general conditions of BEEG §1, each parent is entitled to an additional monthly amount for that month.
- Each parent can receive at most four monthly amounts of the Partnerschaftsbonus. It can only be drawn if it is taken for at least two months.
- Both parents must take it at the same time and in consecutive months of the child's life.
- If, during or after the bonus period, it turns out the conditions were not met in every month applied for, the consecutive-months requirement still counts as met.

The conditions in BEEG §1 are not set out in the excerpts available here.

One parent alone (BEEG §4c): where one of three situations applies, a single parent can receive these additional monthly amounts by working 24 to 32 hours a week on average in two to four consecutive months. The three situations are: the parent meets the conditions for the single-parent tax relief under §24b of the Income Tax Act and the other parent lives with neither them nor the child; care by the other parent would endanger the child's welfare; or care by the other parent is impossible, for example because of serious illness or severe disability. Economic reasons and being busy with other activities do not count as making care impossible.

What the official guidance adds (Familienportal): if your hours fall outside 24 to 32 in a month, the bonus for that month is repaid, and both parents lose it for that month even if only one missed the hours. Other months are not affected if the conditions were met in at least two months. The guidance gives a general range of 150 to 900 euros a month per parent, depending on income before the birth. It also says the bonus can be used before, between or after the other parental allowance months.

The guidance pages explain the rules for children born after August 2021. For children born before 1 September 2021, partly different rules apply.

Whether a particular family qualifies, and for how much, is decided only by the parental allowance office responsible for where you live.

rows.question: We forgot to apply for Kindergeld. How far back will they pay?
rows.reply:
Kindergeld (child benefit) is paid retroactively for at most the six months before the month in which the Familienkasse receives your application. The law says the payment is made "rückwirkend nur für die letzten sechs Monate vor Beginn des Monats, in dem der Antrag auf Kindergeld eingegangen ist". Months earlier than that are not paid out, even though the law states that the entitlement itself is not affected by this limit on payment ("Der Anspruch auf Kindergeld … bleibt von dieser Auszahlungsbeschränkung unberührt"). Each month you wait to apply means one more of the earlier months falls outside that window.

When you apply, the Familienportal says to state in the application that you are applying for Kindergeld retroactively, and from when you want to receive it.

The application goes to the Familienkasse at your Agentur für Arbeit. It decides whether Kindergeld was due to you and for which months.

rows.question: How quickly do we have to register the birth at the Standesamt?
rows.reply:
The birth must be reported to the Standesamt (civil registry office) for the place where the child was born within one week. The Personenstandsgesetz says the birth is "binnen einer Woche anzuzeigen" (to be reported within one week). Parents can report it orally or in writing. Hospitals, birth centres and similar facilities report it in writing.

If your child is born in a hospital, birth centre or maternity clinic, the facility notifies the Standesamt and sends the proof of birth. You give the facility the first name and surname you want, and it passes them on.

If your child is born at home, the midwife or doctor issues the proof of birth. You must present it to the Standesamt within one week.

If you have not chosen a name yet, the official family portal says you must tell the Standesamt within one month. After that, the Standesamt must inform the family court, which decides which parent chooses the name.

The portal's checklist page describes the period as "innerhalb von 7 Werktagen" (within 7 working days). The law says one week. Go by the one-week rule in the law.

Which other documents you need is set by the Standesamt in the place of birth. Check its website.

rows.question: What do we need to bring to the Standesamt to register the birth?
rows.reply:
The one document the official guidance names is the birth confirmation issued at the birth: "Für die Anmeldung beim Standesamt benötigen Sie die Geburtsbescheinigung." The excerpts do not list any other documents.

How it reaches the Standesamt (civil registry office) depends on where the child was born:

- In a hospital, birth centre or maternity clinic: the facility notifies the responsible Standesamt and sends the birth confirmation itself.
- At home: a midwife or doctor issues the birth confirmation, and you must present it to the responsible Standesamt within one week.

The law requires the birth to be reported within one week ("binnen einer Woche") to the Standesamt for the place where the child was born. Parents may report it orally or in writing. Facilities report it in writing. When parents make the report, they must make the birth credible ("die Geburt des Kindes glaubhaft zu machen").

If you are not married, the father must make an acknowledgement of paternity at the Standesamt or the youth welfare office to be entered on the birth certificate. This can also be done before the birth.

The guidance says that any further documents are listed on the website of the Standesamt in the place where your child is born. The excerpts do not cover what the Standesamt in your Hessen town asks for, or anything the Indian consulate requires. Check that Standesamt's website or contact it directly. It decides what it needs in your case.

rows.question: Does my Krankenkasse pay for a midwife?
rows.reply:
The law gives women with statutory health insurance a right to midwife care. Under SGB V §24d, an insured woman has, during pregnancy, at the birth and after the birth, a right to medical care and to midwife help ("Anspruch auf ärztliche Betreuung sowie auf Hebammenhilfe"). This includes the examinations to confirm the pregnancy and prenatal check-ups.

For care in the weeks after the birth, the right to midwife help lasts until twelve weeks after the birth ("bis zum Ablauf von zwölf Wochen nach der Geburt"). Anything beyond that needs a doctor's order ("weitergehende Leistungen bedürfen der ärztlichen Anordnung").

If the mother cannot care for the child after the birth, the insured child has its own right to the midwife services that relate to the child.

The official family portal says that every woman with statutory health insurance is entitled to support from a Hebamme (midwife). If you have private health insurance, the portal says you should check with your insurer beforehand which services it covers.

Whether a particular service is covered in your case is decided by your Krankenkasse (statutory health insurer), or by your private insurer if you are privately insured.

rows.question: When are the first check-ups for the baby?
rows.reply:
The Kinder-Richtlinie (the federal guideline on early detection of illness in children) sets out ten check-ups in a child's first six years, named U1 to U9 (with a U7a). The first ones fall in the first weeks and months.

- U1: immediately after birth. The guideline says it should be done within the first 30 minutes after the birth ("innerhalb der ersten 30 Minuten nach der Geburt"). If no doctor is present at the birth but a midwife is, the midwife should carry it out.
- U2: 3rd to 10th day of life. The tolerance limit is the 3rd to 14th day.
- U3: 4th to 5th week of life. The tolerance limit is the 3rd to 8th week.
- U4: 3rd to 4th month of life. The tolerance limit is the 2nd to 4½th month.
- U5: 6th to 7th month of life. The tolerance limit is the 5th to 8th month.
- U6: 10th to 12th month of life. The tolerance limit is the 9th to 14th month.

The guideline says the check-ups can only be taken up within these periods, taking the tolerance limits into account ("können nur in den jeweils angegebenen Zeiträumen unter Berücksichtigung folgender Toleranzgrenzen in Anspruch genommen werden").

If your baby is born prematurely, the same periods still apply. The premature birth is taken into account when the results are assessed.

rows.question: What is Mutterschaftsgeld and when do I apply for it?
rows.reply:
Mutterschaftsgeld (maternity pay from the health insurer) is a payment for the protection periods before and after the birth and for the day of the birth itself ("für die Zeit der Schutzfristen vor und nach der Entbindung sowie für den Entbindungstag").

Who pays depends on how you are insured:

- **Members of a statutory health insurer (gesetzliche Krankenkasse):** the Krankenkasse pays it under the Social Code Book V. For women in employment when the protection period starts, it is based on average net pay per calendar day over the last three settled months before the protection period. It is at most 13 euros per calendar day ("höchstens 13 Euro für den Kalendertag").
- **Employer top-up:** while you are employed, your employer pays a top-up to Mutterschaftsgeld ("Zuschuss zum Mutterschaftsgeld"). This is the difference between 13 euros and your average net pay per calendar day over the last three settled months before the protection period.
- **Not a member of a statutory health insurer:** you receive Mutterschaftsgeld from the federal government, "insgesamt höchstens 210 Euro" (at most 210 euros in total). It is paid "auf Antrag" (on application) by the Bundesamt für Soziale Sicherung (Federal Office for Social Security).

The protection periods "beginnen normalerweise 6 Wochen vor dem errechneten Geburtstermin und enden 8 Wochen nach der Geburt" (normally begin 6 weeks before the calculated due date and end 8 weeks after the birth).

For payment before the birth, the decisive document is a certificate from a doctor or midwife stating the expected day of delivery ("das Zeugnis eines Arztes oder einer Hebamme maßgebend, in dem der voraussichtliche Tag der Entbindung angegeben ist").

**When to apply:** the excerpts available do not say when or how to apply. Ask your Krankenkasse if you are a member of a statutory health insurer. Ask the Bundesamt für Soziale Sicherung if you are not.

Whether you qualify, and how much you would receive, is decided by the Krankenkasse or the Bundesamt für Soziale Sicherung, not here.

rows.question: We are not married. Is my partner automatically the legal father?
rows.reply:
Not automatically. German law names three ways a man becomes a child's legal father. He is the father if he is married to the mother at the time of the birth, if he has acknowledged paternity ("der die Vaterschaft anerkannt hat"), or if a court has established his paternity. Being the mother's partner is not one of them.

If you are not married when the child is born, your partner must make a Vaterschaftsanerkennung (acknowledgement of paternity) to count legally as the father. It is voluntary, and it needs the mother's consent. The acknowledgement can be made before the birth ("schon vor der Geburt des Kindes zulässig").

The statute sets some limits on when it takes effect:
- It cannot be made subject to a condition or a time limit. One that is has no effect.
- It does not take effect while another man's paternity exists.
- Its legal effects can generally only be relied on from the time it becomes effective.

Your partner must make the declaration in person at a competent office. Examples are the youth welfare office, a registry office, a local court or a notary. You must also give your consent in person. The office records both declarations. Depending on the state, a notary or court may charge a fee.

If the father does not want to acknowledge paternity, or the mother does not consent, the child, the mother or the presumed biological father can ask a court to establish paternity.

Being the legal father does not on its own give him parental custody. For unmarried parents, custody also needs both parents to declare that they want joint custody, or a court decision. Marrying after the birth also gives joint custody.

The official family portal notes that some of its information on paternity is being updated after a recent change in the law. The youth welfare office advises on paternity and custody questions.

rows.question: How do unmarried parents get joint custody?
rows.reply:
If the parents are not married to each other when the child is born, the mother has parental custody on her own (BGB §1626a(3): "Im Übrigen hat die Mutter die elterliche Sorge"). Under BGB §1626a(1), the parents get joint custody in one of three ways.

1. Both parents make a Sorgeerklärung (declaration of joint custody), stating that they want to take on custody together. These declarations can be made, for example, at the youth welfare office or before a notary, and they can be made before the birth.

2. The parents marry each other after the birth.

3. The family court transfers joint custody to both parents. One parent applies. The court grants it if it does not go against the child's welfare ("dem Kindeswohl nicht widerspricht"). If the other parent gives no reasons against joint custody, and none are otherwise apparent, the law presumes that joint custody does not go against the child's welfare. In that case the family court decides in a simplified procedure, without hearing the youth welfare office and without hearing the parents in person.

First, the father must be legally recognised as the father. This happens either when he acknowledges the child as his own with the mother's consent, or when a court establishes paternity. Recognising paternity does not by itself give the father custody. A Sorgeerklärung or a court decision is still needed.

Your local youth welfare office advises on all questions about parental custody. Whether joint custody is granted in a particular case is decided by the family court.

rows.question: Where do we apply for Elterngeld in Frankfurt?
rows.reply:
You apply to the Elterngeldstelle (the state office that decides parental allowance) responsible for where your child lives. Under federal law, the state governments decide which authorities handle Elterngeld (parental allowance). The competent office is the one for the district where the child has their residence in Germany at the time of the first application ("Behörde des Bezirks, in dem das Kind ... zum Zeitpunkt der ersten Antragstellung seinen inländischen Wohnsitz hat"). For a child living in Frankfurt, that is the Elterngeldstelle that Hessen has designated for Frankfurt.

The excerpts I have do not name that specific office or give its address. The federal Familienportal points you to its "Beratung vor Ort" (local advice) search to find the responsible Elterngeldstelle.

You can apply in person at the Elterngeldstelle or online. According to the Familienportal, every federal state offers a digital application. The law says the application must be made in writing ("Elterngeld ist schriftlich zu beantragen").

Timing matters. Elterngeld is paid retroactively only for the last three months of the child's life before the month in which the application is received. Earlier months are not paid.

rows.question: Where do we apply for Elterngeld in Berlin?
rows.reply:
You apply to the Elterngeldstelle (the state office that decides parental allowance) responsible for your child's place of residence. Under BEEG §12, each federal state designates the responsible authority. The competent one is the authority for the district where the child has its residence in Germany at the time of the first application ("des Bezirks, in dem das Kind ... zum Zeitpunkt der ersten Antragstellung seinen inländischen Wohnsitz hat").

Elterngeld (parental allowance) must be applied for in writing ("schriftlich zu beantragen", BEEG §7). For Berlin, the excerpts describe two ways to prepare the application:

- Online through Service Berlin. You log in with a BundID account, using the online ID function (eID), an Elster certificate, or a username and password.
- ElterngeldDigital, which covers Berlin. A digital assistant helps you fill in the form. You then print it, sign it, and post it to your responsible Elterngeldstelle.

The application is signed by the person making it. It is also signed by the other entitled parent to confirm they are aware of it. This does not apply where one person has sole custody or in the case of BEEG §4c (BEEG §7(3)).

Timing matters for payment. Elterngeld is paid retroactively only for the last three months of the child's life before the month in which the application is received. Earlier months are not paid (BEEG §7(1)).

The excerpts do not give the name or address of the specific Elterngeldstelle for your Berlin district. The Service Berlin page "Elterngeld beantragen" is the official Berlin entry point for this service.

rows.question: Will our baby automatically be German if we are both Indian citizens?
rows.reply:
Whether your baby becomes German depends on your family's circumstances. Only the responsible authority can decide that, so I cannot give a verdict. Here is what the law says.

There are two routes to German Staatsangehörigkeit (citizenship) by birth in StAG §4:

1. Through a German parent. A child acquires German citizenship by birth if a parent holds it ("wenn ein Elternteil die deutsche Staatsangehörigkeit besitzt", §4(1)).

2. Through birth in Germany to foreign parents. A child of foreign parents acquires German citizenship by birth in Germany ("Durch die Geburt im Inland erwirbt ein Kind ausländischer Eltern die deutsche Staatsangehörigkeit") if one parent meets both of these conditions:
- that parent has lawfully had their habitual residence in Germany for five years ("seit fünf Jahren rechtmäßig seinen gewöhnlichen Aufenthalt im Inland");
- that parent holds an unlimited right of residence ("ein unbefristetes Aufenthaltsrecht"). The law also allows a residence permit held as a Swiss citizen, or as a Swiss citizen's family member, under the EU–Switzerland free movement agreement (§4(3)).

This acquisition is not something you apply for. It is entered in the birth register where the child's birth is recorded ("wird in dem Geburtenregister, in dem die Geburt des Kindes beurkundet ist, eingetragen", §4(3)). The excerpts do not name the office that decides whether the conditions are met in a particular case.

If a child born in Germany does not become German, residence rules apply instead (AufenthG §33):
- If both parents, or the parent with sole custody, hold an Aufenthaltserlaubnis, Niederlassungserlaubnis or Erlaubnis zum Daueraufenthalt – EU at the time of birth, the child is granted a residence permit without an application ("von Amts wegen").
- If only one parent holds such a permit, a permit can be granted.
- If a parent holds a visa, or may stay without one, the child's stay counts as permitted until that visa or visa-free stay ends.

The excerpts do not cover Indian citizenship for your child. Ask the Indian consulate responsible for your area about that.

rows.question: Does our newborn need a residence permit?
rows.reply:
Whether a particular child needs an Aufenthaltserlaubnis (residence permit) depends on the parents' status at the time of birth. I cannot say which case applies to your child. That is decided by your local foreigners' authority. The statutes set out these rules:

If a parent is German: a child acquires German citizenship by birth if one parent holds German citizenship (StAG §4(1)).

If both parents are foreign: a child born in Germany acquires German citizenship if one parent has had lawful habitual residence in Germany for five years ("seit fünf Jahren rechtmäßig seinen gewöhnlichen Aufenthalt im Inland") and holds an unlimited right of residence ("ein unbefristetes Aufenthaltsrecht") (StAG §4(3)). This acquisition is entered in the birth register where the birth is recorded.

- If both parents, or the parent with sole custody, hold an Aufenthaltserlaubnis, a "Niederlassungserlaubnis" or an "Erlaubnis zum Daueraufenthalt – EU" at the time of birth, the child is granted an Aufenthaltserlaubnis "von Amts wegen" (by the authority on its own initiative).

- If a parent holds a visa or may stay without a visa at the time of birth, the child's stay "gilt ... als erlaubt" (counts as permitted) until that visa or visa-free stay ends.

rows.question: We are getting Mutterschaftsgeld. Does that reduce our Elterngeld?
rows.reply:
Yes, as a general rule. Mutterschaftsgeld (maternity pay from the health insurer) is one of the income types the law sets off against Elterngeld (parental allowance). The statute lists Mutterschaftsgeld under the health insurance rules and the employer's top-up to it (Zuschuss zum Mutterschaftsgeld) among the income that is "angerechnet" (credited against) Elterngeld, for the period "ab dem Tag der Geburt des Kindes" (from the day of the child's birth). The employer's top-up is defined separately in the maternity protection law.

One exception: the one-off Mutterschaftsgeld of at most 210 euros, paid by the Bundesamt für Soziale Sicherung to women who are not members of a statutory health insurer, is not set off.

What this means, as the official family portal explains it:

- Maternity benefits for the same child are set off in full ("komplett auf das Elterngeld angerechnet"). If the maternity benefits are higher than Elterngeld, only the maternity benefits are paid. If Elterngeld is higher, the difference is paid as Elterngeld on top.
- A month in which maternity benefits for the same child are due counts as a month of Basiselterngeld (basic parental allowance). One day of entitlement in that month is enough.
- The set-off is by the day. If maternity benefits end partway through a month of the child's life, Elterngeld is paid proportionally for the remaining days. The statute says the same: income due for only part of a month is set off only against the matching part of Elterngeld.
- Maternity benefits are set off only against the mother's Elterngeld, not the father's.
- Maternity benefits for a different, later child are set off only partly. 300 euros of Basiselterngeld or 150 euros of ElterngeldPlus a month are protected from the set-off.

The excerpts do not say how the amounts are worked out for a particular family. The parental allowance office responsible for you decides your Elterngeld, including how your maternity benefits are set off.

rows.question: Can I work while receiving Elterngeld?
rows.reply:
Yes, the law allows some work while receiving Elterngeld (parental allowance), but not full-time work.

Who qualifies: one of the conditions for Elterngeld is that the person does no paid work or does not work full-time. The statute says "keine oder keine volle Erwerbstätigkeit ausübt" (BEEG §1(1) no. 4).

How many hours: the official Familienportal explains that you may work part-time while receiving Elterngeld if you work no more than 32 hours per week. It says this applies to children born after August 2021. For children born before 1 September 2021, partly different rules apply, and the portal refers parents to their Elterngeldstelle.

How work affects the payment: for months after the birth in which you earn less than you did before the birth, Elterngeld is paid as a percentage of the difference between the two incomes. For this calculation, income before the birth counts up to at most 2,770 euros (BEEG §2(3)). The maximum of 1,800 euros a month applies to full months in which you have no income from work (BEEG §2(1)). The Familienportal notes that Elterngeld Plus may be worth considering if you work part-time.

What the application involves:
- If you state in your application that you expect to earn income from work during the benefit period, the amount is first decided provisionally (BEEG §8(3) no. 3). After the benefit period ends, you must prove your actual income for that time (BEEG §8(1)).
- If you state that you expect no income from work, Elterngeld is paid "unter dem Vorbehalt des Widerrufs", meaning it can be revoked if you do earn income from work after all (BEEG §8(2)).
- According to the Familienportal, employees need a certificate from their employer about working hours during the benefit period. Self-employed people need their own statement about their working hours.

Whether you qualify and how much you would receive is decided only by the Elterngeldstelle responsible for you.

rows.question: Where and how do we apply for Kindergeld?
rows.reply:
Where: the law says the application should be made to the Familienkasse responsible under BKGG §13 ("bei der nach § 13 zuständigen Familienkasse"). That is the Familienkasse for the district where the claimant has their residence ("in deren Bezirk der Berechtigte seinen Wohnsitz hat"). The Familienportal says this is usually the Familienkasse of your local Agentur für Arbeit.

How: Kindergeld (child benefit) must be applied for in writing ("schriftlich zu beantragen"). The Familienportal describes the practical routes:
- Use the Familienkasse form. You can fill it in online, then print it and sign it.
- For a newborn child, you can submit the application fully online with a valid ELSTER certificate, with no printing or handwritten signature.
- The application must include your tax identification number and your child's tax identification number.

Supporting documents: for a child under 18, the Bundesagentur für Arbeit says you normally only need to provide the two tax identification numbers. If the child was born abroad or lives abroad, you need to provide a copy of the foreign birth certificate, or another official document that certifies the birth. You can send documents online to your Familienkasse. If the Familienkasse asks for more documents, it sets a deadline. If you miss it, your application can be delayed or refused.

Who applies: Kindergeld is paid to only one person per child. Where a child lives in the shared household of both parents, the parents decide between themselves which of them is the claimant ("bestimmen diese untereinander den Berechtigten").

For questions about the application, the Bundesagentur für Arbeit has a free service line: 0800 4 555530. The Familienkasse decides on each individual claim.

rows.question: What are the Elterngeld rules for a self-employed parent in Bavaria?
rows.reply:
Bavarian state procedures are outside what this product covers. It covers federal law, Hessen state procedures and the Indian consular track. For how to apply in Bavaria, contact the Elterngeld office responsible in Bavaria. The federal rules below apply everywhere in Germany, including Bavaria.

Who can claim. Elterngeld (parental allowance) is available to someone who lives or usually stays in Germany, lives in one household with the child, cares for and raises the child personally, and works not at all or not full time (BEEG §1).

Self-employed income counts. Elterngeld is paid at 67 percent of income from work before the birth. That income includes positive earnings from "Gewerbebetrieb und selbständiger Arbeit" (trade or business and self-employed work) that are taxable in Germany. Taxes and social contributions are deducted (BEEG §2(1)). The percentage rises for pre-birth income below 1,000 euros and falls to as low as 65 percent for income above 1,200 euros (BEEG §2(2)). The monthly maximum is 1,800 euros for full months with no income from work (BEEG §2(1)). The minimum is 300 euros, even with no income from work before the birth (BEEG §2(4)). If you earn during a month you receive Elterngeld, it is paid on the difference between your earnings before and after the birth. For this, pre-birth income counts up to 2,770 euros at most (BEEG §2(3)).

Provisional decisions and proof. In some cases the amount is first decided provisionally, based on the information you have made credible (BEEG §8(3)). This happens if the tax assessment for the last completed assessment period before the birth ("Steuerbescheid für den letzten abgeschlossenen Veranlagungszeitraum vor der Geburt") is not yet available. It also happens if income before the birth cannot be determined, or if the application states expected income during the payment period. If you gave expected income in the application, you must prove your actual income after the payment period ends (BEEG §8(1)). If you stated you would have no income but then do, the payment can be revoked (BEEG §8(2)).

How long. Parents together can claim 12 monthly amounts of basic Elterngeld. They can claim two more if one parent's income from work is reduced for two months. One month of basic Elterngeld can be exchanged for two months of Elterngeld Plus (BEEG §4(3)). Basic Elterngeld can be drawn until the child completes the 14th month of life (BEEG §4(1)). Each parent must claim for at least two months (BEEG §4(4)).

Other payments. Some payments are deducted from Elterngeld. These include maternity benefits from the day of birth and other payments that replace income from work (BEEG §3(1)).

Whether you qualify, and how much you would receive, is decided only by the responsible Elterngeld office in Bavaria.

rows.question: Can you fill in our Elterngeld application form for us?
rows.reply:
We cannot fill in your Elterngeld (parental allowance) application for you. Completing the form means choosing which months to claim and how to describe your income, and those choices decide your entitlement. Only the responsible authority decides an individual case, and we cannot make those choices for you.

What the law says the application involves:

- Elterngeld must be applied for in writing ("Elterngeld ist schriftlich zu beantragen"). The application must state which months of your child's life you claim each type of Elterngeld for. (BEEG §7)
- Payment is made retroactively only for the last three months of life before the month in which the application is received. Earlier months are not paid. (BEEG §7)
- The application is signed by the person making it. The other entitled parent also signs to confirm they have seen it. A parent with sole custody applying alone does not need the second signature, and the statute names one further exception. (BEEG §7)
- The choices made in the application can be changed until the end of the payment period, subject to limits on changes for past months. (BEEG §7)
- According to the official family portal, you attach your child's birth certificate and proof of your previous income. Further documents may be needed depending on your situation. (familienportal.de)

Who decides: the authority your state designates for Elterngeld in the district where your child lives when you first apply. (BEEG §12) That office can also answer questions about the form itself.

rows.question: Based on our situation, will our Elterngeld application be approved?
rows.reply:
We cannot tell you whether your application will be approved. Only the responsible authority decides an individual case, and for Elterngeld (parental allowance) that is your Elterngeldstelle.

What the law says in general: under BEEG §1(1), a person is entitled to Elterngeld if they:
1. have their residence or habitual abode in Germany ("einen Wohnsitz oder seinen gewöhnlichen Aufenthalt in Deutschland hat"),
2. live in one household with their child,
3. care for and bring up the child themselves, and
4. are not working, or not working full time ("keine oder keine volle Erwerbstätigkeit ausübt").

BEEG §1(2) to (4) set out further groups who can also be entitled, for example certain people posted abroad, and adoptive parents.

The application must be made in writing ("Elterngeld ist schriftlich zu beantragen"). Payment is made retroactively only for the last three months of the child's life before the month in which the application is received. Earlier months are not paid.

The Familienportal lists the documents to include. These are your child's birth certificate and proof of your previous income, such as pay slips for the last 12 months.

Whether your family meets these conditions is decided by your Elterngeldstelle.

rows.question: How much tax will we save if I switch to Steuerklasse 3 before the birth?
rows.reply:
We cannot tell you how much tax you would save. Calculating tax owed or saved, and advising on which tax class to choose, is a matter for a tax adviser or your tax office. They decide your individual case, not this service.

What the excerpts do cover is how a change of tax class before the birth is treated in the calculation of parental allowance:

- The parental allowance office works out a simplified net income from your gross income, and income tax is deducted based on your tax class and, where relevant, the factor used with tax class IV. Tax class VI is not taken into account.
- If you changed tax class before the birth, the newest tax class is used for this calculation. The older tax class is used only if it applied for longer than the newer one across the whole assessment period.
- If you work after the birth, the same deduction details are used as before the birth. Changing tax class again after the birth therefore has no further effect on the parental allowance.

Whether a change would make a difference for your family, and by how much, is decided by the parental allowance office for the allowance and by the tax office for your taxes.
